Bitset operations for shared-memory index sets with iteration, set algebra, and range APIs.

# Purpose
This file defines a header-only template for a fixed-size bit set type. It uses the macros `SET_NAME` and `SET_MAX` to generate a set API with a private type alias, `SET_(t)`, and a group of functions for memory layout, construction, validation, membership tests, iteration, and set operations. The set stores elements in an array of `ulong` words and supports indices in the range `[0, SET_MAX)`. The code also includes support for shared-memory use through `new`, `join`, `leave`, and `delete` functions, so the same set object can be placed in a memory region and used across processes.

The main body of the file implements fast bitwise operations on the set data. It provides functions to insert and remove single elements, test membership, compare sets, and build derived sets such as null, full, singleton, complement, union, intersection, subtraction, and xor. It also provides range-based operations for contiguous index intervals, plus iterators for sparse and constant traversal in increasing order. The implementation is designed for dense sets with a large maximum size, and it uses direct word-level bit manipulation to keep these operations efficient.
